title: Rounding Numbers and Estimating Sums and Differences
seo_title: Grade 4 Rounding and Estimating Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Round numbers to the nearest hundred thousand; estimate the sum and difference of two 5- to 6-digit numbers by rounding the addends to the nearest large place value of the numbers.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 rounding and estimating worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: round to the nearest thousand and hundred thousand, and estimate sums and differences. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Look at the digit to the right: 5 or more rounds up.
key_sub: Estimate: round first, then add or subtract.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To round, find the place you are rounding to and look at the digit just to its right.
  • If that digit is 5 or more, round up. If it is 4 or less, keep the digit. All the digits to the right become 0.
  • To estimate a sum or difference, round each number first, then add or subtract.
  • An estimate tells you if an exact answer is reasonable.

Examples

Example

Round 648,215 to the nearest hundred thousand

Ten thousands digit: 4

Answer: 600,000

Example

Estimate 48,710 + 31,260

50,000 + 30,000

Answer: 80,000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Rounding down at 55 or more rounds up.
Changing digits to the leftOnly the rounding place can change (and carry).
Adding first, rounding laterFor an estimate, round each number first.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 4 ask about rounding?
faq.a: Round numbers to the nearest hundred thousand, and estimate the sum and difference of two 5- to 6-digit numbers by rounding the addends to the nearest large place value of the numbers.
To check that an answer makes sense and to calculate quickly.

faq.q: What is 750,000 rounded to the nearest hundred thousand?
faq.a: 800,000, because the ten thousands digit is 5.
It is not exact, but it should be close.

items.q: Round 1,276 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 1,276 is between 1,000 and 2,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 2. It is 4 or less, so round down. So 1,276 ≈ 1,000.

items.q: Round 2,011 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 2,011 is between 2,000 and 3,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 0. It is 4 or less, so round down. So 2,011 ≈ 2,000.

items.q: Round 6,645 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 6,645 is between 6,000 and 7,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up. So 6,645 ≈ 7,000.

items.q: Round 5,589 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 5,589 is between 5,000 and 6,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 5. It is 5 or more, so round up. So 5,589 ≈ 6,000.

items.q: Round 4,500 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 4,500 is exactly halfway between 4,000 and 5,000. A number exactly halfway rounds up. So 4,500 ≈ 5,000.

items.q: 3,129 ≈ ☐ when it is rounded to the nearest 1,000. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 3,129 is between 3,000 and 4,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 1. It is 4 or less, so round down. So 3,129 ≈ 3,000.

items.q: Round 85,984 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 85,984 is between 85,000 and 86,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 9. It is 5 or more, so round up. So 85,984 ≈ 86,000.

items.q: Round 17,843 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 17,843 is between 17,000 and 18,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 8. It is 5 or more, so round up. So 17,843 ≈ 18,000.

items.q: Round 6,457 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 6,457 is between 6,000 and 7,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down. Do not round in two steps (6,457 → 6,500 → 7,000). Round the number you started with. So 6,457 ≈ 6,000.

items.q: Round 53,972 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 53,972 is between 53,000 and 54,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 9. It is 5 or more, so round up. So 53,972 ≈ 54,000.

items.q: Round 9,615 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 9,615 is between 9,000 and 10,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up. The thousands digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 thousands. Rename 10 thousands as 1 ten thousand: 9,000 + 1,000 = 10,000. So 9,615 ≈ 10,000.

items.q: Which number rounds to 3,000 when you round it to the nearest 1,000?
items.e: Numbers from 2,500 to 3,499 round to 3,000. 2,684 is in that range. 3,500 rounds to 4,000.

items.q: 2,499 ≈ ☐ when it is rounded to the nearest 1,000. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 2,499 is between 2,000 and 3,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down. Do not round in two steps (2,499 → 2,500 → 3,000). Round the number you started with. So 2,499 ≈ 2,000.

items.q: Round 39,600 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 39,600 is between 39,000 and 40,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up. The thousands digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 thousands. Rename 10 thousands as 1 ten thousand: 39,000 + 1,000 = 40,000. So 39,600 ≈ 40,000.

items.q: 99,600 ≈ ☐ when it is rounded to the nearest 1,000. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 99,600 is between 99,000 and 100,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up. The thousands digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 thousands. Rename 10 thousands as 1 ten thousand: 99,000 + 1,000 = 100,000. So 99,600 ≈ 100,000.

items.q: What is the smallest whole number that rounds to 8,000 when you round it to the nearest 1,000?
items.e: Numbers from 7,500 to 8,499 round to 8,000. 7,499 rounds down to 7,000, so the smallest is 7,500.

items.q: Round 6,348 to the nearest 10, the nearest 100 and the nearest 1,000. Which list is correct?
items.e: Always around the number you started with, 6,348. Nearest 10: the ones digit is 8, so 6,350. Nearest 100: the tens digit is 4, so 6,300. Nearest 1,000: the hundreds digit is 3, so 6,000. Do not round 6,350 again to get 6,400 and then 7,000.

items.q: Round 3,482 to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 3,482 is between 3,400 and 3,500. The digit to the right of the hundreds place is 8, so round up. Answer: 3,500.

items.q: Round 96,500 to the nearest thousand.

items.q: Round 499,999 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest thousand: 499,999 is between 499,000 and 500,000. The digit to the right of the thousands place is 9, so round up. The thousands digit is 9, so adding 1 thousand regroups: 499,000 + 1,000 = 500,000. Answer: 500,000.
